newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Malaysian firm to build $3.5 billion cargo hub.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian firm to build $3.5 billion cargo hub.

text.p: Malaysia-based Dragon Gold has agreed to develop a $3.5 billion industrial free trade zone and cargo hub in central Cambodia, a company representative said on Tuesday.
"The ink just dried on the deal Monday...," Iain Gray told Reuters.
A statement from the Cambodian cabinet said the company had formed a joint venture with the government to create the cargo hub, tourism centre and industrial zone under the name Transglobal Ltd.

Gray said the deal included developing an unused airport in Kompong Chhnang province, developing a 12,500-hectare (30,000 acre) free trade and industrial zone and an eco-tourism site, and creating a telecommunications and road network.
He said the deal had backers from the United States, Australian, Malaysia and Germany.
The airport facility was built during the brutal 1975-79 rule of the Khmer Rouge.
Tens of thousands of Cambodians were said to have lost their lives in building the site, located an hour's drive northwest of the capital.
A cargo analyst said the airport had the longest and best runway in Cambodia was ideally located near the Tonle Sap river, rail links and planned highways.
